# The EXPRESS schema language {#sec-express}

Every entity that can appear in a STEP file is declared in a schema written in EXPRESS, the data modelling language defined by ISO 10303-11 [@iso10303-11].
You do not need to write EXPRESS to use STEP, but being able to read it turns the standard from an opaque wall of text into a precise reference.

## A first schema

```{#lst-express .default lst-cap="An EXPRESS declaration of the placement entity from @sec-anatomy"}
ENTITY axis2_placement_3d
  SUBTYPE OF (placement);
  axis      : OPTIONAL direction;
  ref_direction : OPTIONAL direction;
DERIVE
  p : LIST [3:3] OF direction := build_axes(axis, ref_direction);
WHERE
  WR1 : self\placement.location.dim = 3;
  WR2 : (NOT (EXISTS (axis))) OR (axis.dim = 3);
  WR3 : (NOT (EXISTS (ref_direction))) OR (ref_direction.dim = 3);
  WR4 : (NOT (EXISTS (axis))) OR (NOT (EXISTS (ref_direction))) OR
        (cross_product(axis, ref_direction).magnitude > 0.0);
END_ENTITY;
```

Compare this with instance `#4` in @lst-minimal: the attribute order in the file follows the declaration, including the `location` inherited from the supertype `placement`.
